The short grievance of the petitioners is that the lands of the petitioners have been acquired by the State under the Karnataka Industrial Area Development Act, 1966 (for short, 'KIAD Act') as regards which the award has been passed under the Land Acquisition Act 1894 and not under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short, the 'Act of 2013').
3.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The submission of Sri.Mahantesh Patil, learned counsel for the petitioners is that the very notification issued under sub-section (4) of Section 28 of the KIAD Act had categorically indicated that any developments which were made to the property subject matter of the proposed acquisition would not be taken into consideration for the purpose of awardal of compensation under the Act of 2013 and as such, on that basis, he submits that insofar as the lands acquired are concerned,
compensation is NC: 2024:KHC-K:6938 required to be paid under the Act of 2013.
The award could not have been passed under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and as such, the relief sought for are required to be granted.

4. Sri A.M.Nagral, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2-SLAO KIADB would submit that what is excluded under the said notification is the improvement made post the notification and that exclusion will not come to the benefit of the petitioners insofar as claiming compensation as regards the land under the Act of 2013 and as such, he submits that Act of 2013 would not be applicable for the purpose of calculation of compensation in respect to the lands acquired.

5. Heard Sri.Mahantesh Patil, learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri.A.M.Nagral, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 - SLAO KIADB and perused the papers.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:6938 6.

Though a very novel argument has been addressed by Sri.A.M.Nagral, learned counsel for respondent No.2 - SLAO KIADB, I am unable to accept the same when the notification itself indicates that development put up on the land will be excluded for the purpose of consideration while passing an award and that consideration is to be made under the Act of 2013, the same would necessarily imply that the compensation as regards the lands and the improvements already made Sundar Kopparakara And Ors vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19661066/
5 prior to the notification being issued would be done in terms of the Act of 2013.

sentences.text: Admittedly, the notification in these matters has been issued on 07.11.2017, much after the 2013 Act came into force on 01.01.2014.
It is but required that compensation is required to be paid as regards the lands acquired post the Act of 2013, coming into force under the Act of 2013.

7. Hence, I pass the following:
NC: 2024:KHC-K:6938 ORDER i.
Writ petitions are allowed.
ii. The reliefs sought for are moulded.

Respondent No.2-SLAO KIADB, is directed to pass an additional award under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation,
Resettlement Act, 2013 after giving due deduction to the earlier award passed under Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
iii.

Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation,
Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Both the awards shall be read in a composite manner.
iv. The amount awarded under the impugned award shall be disbursed to the petitioners if not deposited in the Court.
If already deposited in the Court, the petitioners would be entitled to make an application - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:6938 for release of the said monies without prejudice to their rights.

v. As regards the additional award to be  passed under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation, Resettlement Act, 2013, the respondent No.1 is directed to complete the process of preparing and finalizing the award within a period of 90 days from the date of receipt of copy of the order.
